title: kernel-trace-pruning-and-safety-procedures-2026
author: Asha Patel
body:
Summary:
This playbook documents the design, operational controls, and incident procedures for kernel-level trace pruning used by the runtime tracing pipeline. The goal is to limit telemetry volume and remove sensitive or high-cardinality fields while preserving causal fidelity for performance debugging and regressions. This is a prescriptive, production-oriented document intended for runtime, observability, and security engineers.

Background and motivation:
- The runtime emits kernel-level traces (scheduling decisions, kernel selection, KV cache events) at high cardinality. Left unpruned, trace volume increases storage costs and risks leaking customer data in verbose argument payloads.
- We operate two primary tracing tiers: "fidelity" traces (full context for on-demand debugging) and "operational" traces (pruned, aggregated, low-cost).
- This document defines pruning rules, safety checks, rollout and rollback steps, and incident response.

Goals:
1. Ensure pruning reduces telemetry volume by >= 60% in standard production mixes without losing causal linkages required for latency attribution.
2. Prevent storage of PII or customer payloads in long-term trace stores.
3. Make pruning configurable per-cluster/cohort with safe defaults and transparent metrics.
4. Provide an operational runbook for debugging failures or regressions introduced by pruning.

Scope and exclusions:
- Applies to services: runtime-trace-collector, kernel-hint-propagator, trace-pruner-service, trace-archiver.
- Does NOT replace application-level PII redaction (owners must still instrument sanitizers).
- Excludes ephemeral debug captures created by debug on-demand (those follow different retention).

Architecture overview:
- Ingest: runtime nodes push proto-packed spans to runtime-trace-collector over gRPC (path: /v1/trace/spans).
- Pre-processor: kernel-hint-propagator annotates spans with metadata (kernel id, shard id, priority class).
- Pruner: trace-pruner-service applies declarative rules (field whitelist/blacklist, regex masks, size caps, sample/retain decisions) and emits two outputs: operational-traces (kafka topic) and fidelity-traces (S3 bucket if debug-on-demand is enabled).
- Archival: trace-archiver moves fidelity-traces to cold storage subject to access controls and audit logging.

Key configuration primitives (policy model):
- allow-list-fields: list of field paths preserved verbatim.
- redact-patterns: list of regex patterns applied to values (replaced with <REDACTED>).
- max-span-bytes: integer - truncation cap per span payload.
- cohort-sampling: map of cohort -> sample_rate (0.0 - 1.0).
- link-preserve-strategy: [retain-ids|compact-ids|regen] - how parent/child ids are preserved across pruned traces.

Operational thresholds and SLOs (table):
| Signal | Threshold | Owner | Notes |
|-------|----------:|-------|------|
| runtime.trace.pruner.drop_rate | <= 0.05 (5%) | runtime-observability | Fraction of spans dropped after pruning vs received (target <=5%) |
| runtime.trace.pruner.latency_p50 | <= 30ms | runtime-observability | P50 processing time for prune operation |
| runtime.trace.pruner.latency_p99 | <= 200ms | runtime-observability | P99 allowed for low traffic; alert if sustained >500ms |
| runtime.trace.pruner.pii_detection_alerts | 0 | security | Any PII detection triggers immediate review |
| storage.traces.ingest_bytes_per_min | project-dependent | infra-sre | Ensure per-cluster quota not exceeded |

Notes on the table: SLOs are monitored via prometheus metrics described below. Alert rules live in /confluence/eng-sre/alerts/trace-pruner-alerts (see related_pages).

Pruning rules (examples):
1. Field-level redaction: for any field matching request.input.text and request.output.completions.*.text, apply redact-patterns for email, phone, credit-card. Example regex: (?:\b\d{12,19}\b)|(?:\b[\w.-]+@[\w.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}\b).
2. High-cardinality dims: remove or hash values for fields tagged dim.cardinality.high (e.g., session_id, ephemeral_token). Keep a 64-bit truncated hash for causal joins.
3. Size capping: if span total bytes > max-span-bytes, strip non-essential nested structures in this order: stack_traces -> raw_payload -> metrics_payload. Add annotation: pruner.reason=truncated_size.
4. Link preservation: When link-preserve-strategy=compact-ids, replace parent_id/trace_id with shorter digest and add mapping to a transient lookup service (ttl 6h) to reconstruct if fidelity capture requested.

Metrics and alerts (metric names):
- runtime.trace.pruner.spans_in_total (counter)
- runtime.trace.pruner.spans_out_operational (counter)
- runtime.trace.pruner.spans_out_fidelity (counter)
- runtime.trace.pruner.drop_rate (gauge)
- runtime.trace.pruner.processing_latency_seconds (histogram)
- runtime.trace.pruner.pii_detection_count (counter)
- runtime.trace.pruner.hash_collision_warnings (counter)

Alerting guidelines (examples):
- P1: "PII detection in pruned output" -> page security and runtime-observability; block exports to long-term store; set retention of the offending batch to quarantine; open incident.
- P2: "Pruner drop_rate > 0.1 for > 5 minutes" -> page runtime-oncall; increase logging sampling; consider rollback to previous policy.
- P3: "Processing latency p99 > 1s sustained" -> page infra-sre then runtime; consider autoscaling trace-pruner replicas, adjust batch window.

Runbook: Recovering from an unsafe prune configuration (e.g., over-redaction, data loss, PII leak)
1. Detect: Pager triggers from pii_detection or customer report.
2. Quarantine: Disable archiver job for the affected cluster: kubectl -n traces scale deployment/trace-archiver --replicas=0.
3. Snapshot: Export the candidate raw spans from kafka topic trace-raw-{cluster} to s3://quarantine/{incident-id}/raw/ using trace-tools kafka-dump --topic trace-raw-{cluster} --to-s3 s3://... --start-offset X --end-offset Y.
4. Audit: Run trace-pruner-tool inspect --policy current --sample s3://quarantine/{incident-id}/raw/ --rules to enumerate exactly which rule triggered redactions. Save output to /var/incident/{id}/audit.json.
5. Rollback policy: If over-redaction caused debugging regressions, revert pruner policy to last_good: kubectl -n traces set configmap trace-pruner-policy --from-file=last_good_policy.yaml.
6. Reingest: For cases where fidelity data was intended to be retained but got pruned, follow the reingest path only when security approves. Use trace-tools replay --from-s3 s3://quarantine/{incident-id}/raw/ --to-topic trace-replay-{cluster}.
7. Postmortem: Create incident with label trace-pruner and include timeline, root cause, and corrective actions.

Safe rollout checklist (for policy changes):
1. Create policy in git: infra/tracing/policies/{cluster}/{policy-name}.yaml. Include allow-list-fields and redact-patterns.
2. Unit test: run make test-pruner (includes regex correctness and hash collision checks).
3. Staging deploy: deploy to staging cluster, monitor metrics for 24h. Check drop_rate and processing latency.
4. Shadow deploy: enable policy in shadow mode: pruner.shadow=true -> metrics emitted but not applied. Observe comparisons for 48h.
5. Canary: Apply policy with cohort-sampling 0.05 for low-risk cohort. Monitor for 2 business days.
6. Full rollout: increase cohort-sampling progressively to 1.0 in 3 steps (0.2, 0.6, 1.0) with at least 12h observation windows.
7. Post-rollout audit: run an automated pii-scan across operational-traces for 72h.

Testing guidance and synthetic checks:
- Unit tests for regex must include >200 negative and positive samples (store in infra/tracing/tests/regex_corpus.csv).
- Fuzz tests for hash collisions: run hash-fuzz-runner --rounds 1M weekly. Alert if collision rate > 1e-6.
- Integration: run trace-simulator to replay 24h of production-shaped traffic through the pruner to validate volume reduction targets.

Developer diagnostics (quick commands):
- Validate current policy: kubectl -n traces exec deploy/trace-pruner -- trace-pruner-cli validate /etc/pruner/policy.yaml --output concise
- Dry-run sample: trace-pruner-cli dryrun --policy /etc/pruner/policy.yaml --input s3://samples/production_day1.json --mode shadow --report-summary /tmp/pruner-dryrun-summary.json
- Inspect recent pruner metrics: grafana dashboard "Trace Pruner Overview" -> panels: drop_rate, latency histogram, pii alerts.

Common failure modes and mitigations:
- Symptom: sudden drop in fidelity-traces count. Cause: cohort-sampling default 0.0 due to config bug. Mitigation: set cohort-sampling for debug cohort to 0.02 and re-evaluate; hotfix config map.
- Symptom: increased p99 prune latency. Cause: oversized batches from trace-collector. Mitigation: reduce batch window at collector: TRACE_COLLECTOR_BATCH_MS from 5000 -> 2000, redeploy collector.
- Symptom: stray PII in operational storage. Cause: missing redact-pattern. Mitigation: block export, add pattern, run re-scan, escalate to security.

Release notes (recent change summary):
- 2026-01-18: Initial published playbook and safe defaults (max-span-bytes=8192, default cohort-sampling=0.1 for operational).
- 2026-02-22: Added compact-ids link preservation option with transient lookup service; introduced pii_detection_count metric and quarantine flow.

Appendix: sample policy (YAML)
---
# Example: infra/tracing/policies/prod/prune_policy_v3.yaml
allow-list-fields:
  - trace_id
  - kernel.id
  - kernel.priority_class
redact-patterns:
  - email: '(?:\\b[\\w.-]+@[\\w.-]+\\.[A-Za-z]{2,}\\b)'
  - credit_card: '(?:\\b\\d{12,19}\\b)'
max-span-bytes: 8192
cohort-sampling:
  default: 0.15
  debug-cohort: 0.02
link-preserve-strategy: compact-ids
---
